elements.element: This Agreement is governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause expressly provides that the Agreement “shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York.”

elements.element: The parties submit disputes to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state courts located in New York County, New York.
elements.evidence: Although the added sentence expressly submits each party to those courts, the retained provision requires covered “Disputes” to be resolved by binding arbitration and therefore prevents the New York state courts from having exclusive adjudicatory jurisdiction.

elements.element: The parties submit disputes to the exclusive jurisdiction of the federal courts located in New York County, New York.
elements.evidence: Although the added sentence expressly submits each party to those courts, the retained mandatory-arbitration provision requires covered “Disputes” to be resolved by arbitration. It also permits award confirmation in any competent state or federal court, including a court in the federal judicial district where the losing party resides, contradicting exclusivity in New York County.

elements.element: This Agreement is governed by the laws of Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause selects New York law, not any fallback governing law.

elements.element: Disputes are submitted to courts in the forum corresponding to the selected fallback law: Delaware courts, California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause names New York County courts and retains mandatory arbitration; it does not select any corresponding fallback court forum.

result.reason: The redline correctly adopts New York law but does not establish an effective exclusive New York court forum because the mandatory-arbitration provision remains operative and award confirmation is expressly permitted in courts outside New York County. The resulting dispute-resolution provisions conflict, so neither the complete preferred position nor a fallback package is achieved.
